editor_note: All six rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. They keep the bounded-integer and continuous-variable caveat with error 4710 ("inteira com limites inferior e superior explícitos"), render "Breaking changes" as "Alterações incompatíveis", keep the old-to-new value mapping and the unchanged default of 3, and keep the None/4712 condition.

The rewritten entry 28 says what the English says. The QPU time is still "mínimo e quase constante", the reason is still "apenas uma rodada de QAOA", and the parameters are still "obtidos em uma CPU". Nothing here would mislead a learner. The one problem is a naming mismatch: entry 28 writes "problema market split" in lowercase, while every other entry on the page capitalizes it as "problema Market Split" (entries 24, 25, 29, 58 and 62). The caption should match the section heading it sits under.

examples.source: Performance metrics for different instances of the market split problem.
examples.translation: Métricas de desempenho para diferentes instâncias do problema market split.
examples.suggested: Métricas de desempenho para diferentes instâncias do problema Market Split.
examples.why: Everywhere else in the file the problem name is capitalized as "Market Split" (the heading in entry 24, the body in 25 and 29, the changelog in 58, the tips in 62). The lowercase form in this caption makes the name inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (40, 41, 44) keep the English meaning. The ibm_miami figures (below 10% at width 9 / 10 qubits, Orbit near 80–90%), the ibm_kingston ~15% at widths approaching 60, the calibration caveat and N = 50 / 51 qubits all match the source. One terminology problem: entries 41 and 44 write "bitstring oculta", but the rest of the page (entries 25, 46, 65) uses "string de bits oculta". examples.translation: à medida que a largura da bitstring oculta cresce
examples.suggested: à medida que a largura da string de bits oculta cresce
examples.why: The rest of the page says 'string de bits oculta' (entries 25, 46, 65). These rewritten entries switch to 'bitstring', which makes the term inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: To preserve QPU time, this tutorial does not rerun a size sweep.
examples.translation: Para preservar tempo de QPU, este tutorial não executa novamente uma varredura de tamanhos.
examples.suggested: Para economizar tempo de QPU, este tutorial não repete a varredura de tamanhos.
examples.why: 'Preservar tempo' is a calque. In Portuguese you save time ('economizar'), and 'repete a varredura' reads more naturally.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful. In [72], 'porta CNOT com Q como controle e seu próprio qubit como alvo' keeps the same control and target as the English, and in [73], 'agrupar os termos acima de acordo com os resultados das medições nos qubits A e Q' matches the source, with 'porta'/'emaranha' used the same way as in the rest of the page.

None of the three rewritten entries (53, 78, 87) would mislead a learner. Entry 53 keeps the reproducibility condition with "fixe a opção `seed_transpiler`", and entry 87 keeps all four option names and both goals ("qualidade da solução e no tempo de execução"). The one slip is in entry 78. There "addressed by variable name" means the solution is accessed or indexed by variable name, and it became "indicada pelo nome da variável", which is vague. A native editor would write "acessada pelo nome da variável".

examples.source: Only the first solution is considered here, addressed by variable name.
examples.translation: Aqui, apenas a primeira solução é considerada, indicada pelo nome da variável.
examples.suggested: Aqui, apenas a primeira solução é considerada, acessada pelo nome da variável.
examples.why: 'Addressed' here means accessed or indexed (the solution dict is keyed by variable name). 'Indicada' is vague and does not say how the reader gets at the values, so 'acessada' (or 'indexada') is clearer.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 60 is accurate and does not mislead. "Qiskit Function" correctly stays in English, and "Avalie" is a reasonable rendering of "Benchmark". The one problem is "fidelidade do processo QFT". It splits up the fixed technical term "process fidelity" (fidelidade de processo) and reads as "the fidelity of the QFT process". The standard Portuguese wording is "fidelidade de processo da QFT", which also gives QFT (transformada) its feminine article.

examples.source: Benchmark QFT process fidelity with Orbit, a Qiskit Function by Quantum Elements
examples.translation: Avalie a fidelidade do processo QFT com o Orbit, uma Qiskit Function da Quantum Elements
examples.suggested: Avalie a fidelidade de processo da QFT com o Orbit, uma Qiskit Function da Quantum Elements
examples.why: 'Process fidelity' is a set metric term, 'fidelidade de processo'. Writing 'fidelidade do processo QFT' makes 'processo QFT' sound like the thing being measured instead of naming the metric. QFT (transformada de Fourier quântica) takes the feminine article 'da'.

editor_note: Entry 12 is faithful and reads naturally: "frustration is compounded globally" becomes "essa frustração se agrava globalmente", the random positive/negative "forças de interação $J_{ij}$" and the triangular-arrangement caveat are kept, and the rendering matches "força de acoplamento" in entry 16.

None of the 23 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The counts (300 PUBs, 921.600 shots, 60 PUBs per N), the O(n^2) vs O(n) argument in [17] and the troubleshooting advice in [32] and [67] all match the English. Entry [5] has a half-translated calque, "três jobs do Runtime Batch child", although the same paragraph and the rest of the page say "job filho". "transpiler" is left in English in [42] and [56], while [33] uses "transpilador". Entry [67] points to "a seção de Setup", but that heading is rendered as "Configuração" on this page, so a reader looking for "Setup" won't find it.
